title: 機能テストPASSのみを受け入れ基準にすると、レビュー由来の受け入れ制約に違反するAgent Patchの約3分の1が合格扱いになる
summary: SWE-Gate builds 303 repository-level repair instances from 75 Python projects, pairing functional tests with acceptance constraints derived from real pull-request reviews (style, architecture, and non-functional expectations reviewers actually enforce). Of 644 agent repairs that pass the functional tests, 221 (~34%) violate the review-derived constraints. The mechanism: agent pipelines and benchmarks that gate on functional test passage alone systematically accept patches human reviewers would reject, so auto-promotion/auto-merge on green tests and functional-only self-verification both overestimate patch acceptability. This is distinct from F18 (tests pass but build/runtime breaks — an execution gap) and K10 (benchmark-vs-repo performance gap): here the artifact is functionally correct yet unacceptable, and the gap is quantified at the gating layer (He et al., arXiv:2609.04167, 2026-09-03).

evidence.title: SWE-Gate: Passing Functional Tests Is Not Enough for Software Engineering Agents
evidence.summary: 303 repo-level instances from 75 Python projects with review-derived constraint tests: 221 of 644 functionally-passing agent repairs fail the review constraints, showing functional-only evaluation substantially overestimates real-world patch acceptability.
